title: Class 12 module manifest
description: Schema for a module.json. This file is documentation of intent only -- the host does not load a JSON-schema library at runtime. The real enforcement lives in validate.mjs, hand-rolled, so the host has one fewer dependency between a bad manifest and a refusal. Keep the two in agreement by hand; check-registry.mjs is what proves they agree.

id.description: Lowercase, digits and hyphens only. This id is also the table prefix (m_<id>_) and the route prefix (/api/m/<id>/), so a bad id is not a style problem -- it is a boundary problem.

title.description: What shows on the tab. Free text, but not empty -- an empty tab label is a bug the host should not have to guess at.

version.description: The module's own semver. Bumped by the module author, not the host.

hostApi.description: The semver of the host API this module was BUILT against. Compared to the host's own version at load time -- a major mismatch refuses to load, because a module written for a different major API version is reading a contract that no longer holds.

tables.description: Table names this module creates. Every one must start with m_<id>_. A module that names a table outside its own prefix has stepped outside the one boundary Postgres can enforce for it.

routes.description: API paths this module mounts. Every one must start with /api/m/<id>/. A route outside that prefix can shadow or hijack another module's endpoint or a host endpoint, and the collision is invisible until two modules are installed together.

zones.description: Which document zones (Class 10) this module's bound search may read. May be empty. This is the only list that controls what searchFiles the host injects -- a module cannot ask for a zone at runtime that is not declared here.

dependsOn.description: Module ids this module's migrations must run after. May be empty. Used to topologically sort load and migration order -- never to import another module's code directly.

permissions.description: Capabilities this module asks the host for, from a FIXED enum the host defines. A permission string outside this enum is invalid, not ignored -- an unknown permission is what a module built for a newer host looks like, and ignoring it means running that module with fewer restrictions than its author intended.
